story.iWant: to combine all analysis components into complete decision logic
story.soThat: the API returns a comprehensive YES/NO answer with context
story.tasks: - Task 1: Create API route handler at /app/api/check-rain/route.ts - Task 2: Integrate OpenWeather API forecast fetching - Task 3: Integrate rain probability calculation - Task 4: Integrate rain window and safe window detection - Task 5: Build response based on decision logic - Task 6: Implement error handling and HTTP status mapping - Task 7: Manual testing and validation

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: 1. YES/NO decision is based on max probability (≥50% threshold) 2. For YES answers: rain windows, peak details, and safe windows are included 3. For NO answers: only probability is included 4. Close call messaging is added for 40-49% probability range 5. Response format matches the API contract defined in PRD 6. All data is properly formatted for frontend consumption

doc.title: Epic 2: Weather Intelligence Engine
doc.snippet: Acceptance criteria specify YES/NO decision based on ≥50% threshold, conditional response structure (YES includes details, NO includes probability only), close call flag for 40-49% range. Technical notes emphasize generateDecision() orchestrator function combining all analysis components.

doc.title: Story 2.5: Implement Safe Window Calculation
doc.snippet: Provides calculateSafeWindows(rainWindows, forecastEndTime) function accepting RainWindow[] and returning SafeWindow[] with Date objects. Filters gaps <1 hour, handles "after rain" safe window. Returns Date objects requiring formatTimeRange() conversion to strings for API response.

file.reason: Main entry point for fetching weather forecast. Returns location, lat, lon, and forecast data with 3-hour intervals. Throws OpenWeatherError with standardized error codes for error handling.
Custom error class with code (ErrorCode), message, and optional statusCode properties. Used for consistent error handling across OpenWeather API integration.
Parses OpenWeatherResponse into ParsedForecast[] array with normalized data (probability 0-100, amount in inches, intensity classification). Returns first 8 periods (24 hours) in 3-hour intervals.
Main entry point for rain probability calculation. Returns RainProbabilityResult with maxProbability, peakTime, peakHourData, willRain (≥50% threshold), and closeCall (40-49% flag) fields.
Detects continuous rain periods with probability ≥40%. Returns RainWindow[] array with start/end Date objects. Used to identify when rain occurs in the 24-hour forecast.

Calculates clear periods between rain windows. Accepts RainWindow[] and forecastEndTime, returns SafeWindow[] array with Date objects. Filters gaps <1 hour, includes "after rain" safe window if ≥1 hour.
Formats Date objects to 12-hour AM/PM time strings (e.g., "2:00 PM - 5:00 PM"). Reuse this function to convert RainWindow/SafeWindow Date objects to API response strings.
Request interface with location string field. Use for parsing POST request body.

Current interface returns location, lat, lon, and forecast array. Story 2.6 must UPDATE this interface to match tech spec: add willRain, probability, rainWindows, peakTime, intensity, amount, safeWindows, closeCall fields.
Error response interface with error (ErrorCode) and message fields. Use for standardized error handling in API route.
Interface with time (Date), timestamp (number), probability (0-100), intensity (string), amount (inches), temperature, and description fields. Input type for rain analysis modules.

node.reason: Next.js framework for App Router API routes. Use export async function POST(request: Request) pattern for /app/api/check-rain/route.ts handler.
TypeScript strict mode enabled. All types must be explicitly declared, no 'any' types permitted.

story-context.constraints: - Next.js 16 App Router conventions: Export async function POST(request: Request) from route.ts - TypeScript strict mode: No 'any' types, explicit type declarations required - Stateless architecture (ADR-002): No caching, fresh API call every request - Native Fetch API (ADR-005): No axios or HTTP libraries - 5-second timeout per NFR-P2 (handled by OpenWeather module) - Single retry on 5xx errors (handled by OpenWeather module) - Performance target: <2 seconds total response time (~910ms typical) - Error handling: Map OpenWeatherError to appropriate HTTP status codes (404, 500, 504) - Return standardized ErrorResponse for all error scenarios - Decision threshold: ≥50% probability = YES (willRain true), <50% = NO (willRain false) - Close call detection: 40-49% probability sets closeCall flag true - Conditional response structure: YES includes all details, NO includes probability only - Time formatting: Use formatTimeRange() to convert Date objects to "HH:MM AM/PM" strings - API route path: /app/api/check-rain/route.ts (create new file)

interface.name: RainCheckResponse (Updated for Story 2.6)
interface.signature: interface RainCheckResponse { willRain: boolean; probability: number; rainWindows?: RainWindow[]; peakTime?: string; intensity?: string; amount?: string; safeWindows?: SafeWindow[]; closeCall: boolean; }

tests.standards: Manual endpoint testing using curl or Postman. No automated unit tests (deferred to Epic 5 per tech spec). TypeScript compilation validation (npm run type-check) and ESLint validation (npm run lint) required. End-to-end testing via POST requests to /api/check-rain with various locations and scenarios.
tests.locations: will-it-rain/app/api/check-rain/route.ts (API route to be created) will-it-rain/lib/*.test-manual.ts (existing manual test files)
tests.ideas: - Test YES answer scenario with high probability location (≥50%) - verify response includes rainWindows, peakTime, intensity, amount, safeWindows fields (AC1, AC2) - Test NO answer scenario with low probability location (<40%) - verify response includes only probability field (AC3) - Test close call scenario with moderate probability (40-49%) - verify closeCall flag is true (AC4) - Test error handling: invalid location (404), API failures (500), timeout (504), malformed request (400) - verify ErrorResponse format (AC5) - Test response format validation - ensure matches RainCheckResponse interface exactly (AC5) - Test time formatting - verify all times use 12-hour AM/PM format via formatTimeRange() (AC6) - Test edge cases: empty rain windows, single rain window, multiple rain windows, no rain at all - Test HTTP status codes: 200 (success), 400 (bad request), 404 (location not found), 500 (API failure), 504 (timeout) - Verify performance: response time <2 seconds for typical requests - Integration test: curl POST to /api/check-rain with { "location": "Seattle" } and verify complete response structure
